title: U.S. Bank National Association v. Black Plaza Management, LLC (CPLR 3215(c) Abandonment of Foreclosure Claim)
jurisdiction: Supreme Court of the State of New York, Appellate Division, Second Department
amount: Foreclosure claim against Black Plaza Management dismissed as abandoned; costs awarded to Black Plaza
summary: The Appellate Division, Second Department modified a Supreme Court, Queens County order and held that U.S. Bank National Association abandoned its foreclosure claim against defaulted defendant Black Plaza Management, LLC by waiting until December 2019, well over a year after Black Plaza's default in a 2017-filed action, to move for a default judgment. A four-judge panel found the bank's delay violated CPLR 3215(c)'s mandatory one-year window and rejected its explanations as insufficient, dismissing the claim against Black Plaza and awarding it costs.
significance: The ruling is a reminder that CPLR 3215(c)'s one-year deadline applies with equal, mandatory force to commercial mortgage defendants as it does in the high-volume residential foreclosure context where the rule is more commonly litigated. CMBS trustees, portfolio lenders, and special servicers managing large foreclosure dockets should treat the deadline as a hard compliance trigger on every defaulted defendant, not just an administrative afterthought, since an otherwise valid and undisputed mortgage claim was dismissed here solely for missing it.
